chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Isa ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Ali ibn Hisan, from Abu Ayoob, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, why is the Sun hotter than the moon?' He said, 'Indeed, God, the Blessed and Exalted, created the Sun from the light of fire and pure water, layer upon layer, until it became seven layers, then He clothed it with a garment of fire; from this it became hotter than the moon.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, and the moon?' He said, 'Indeed, God, the Exalted, created the moon from the light of fire and pure water, layer upon layer, until it became seven layers, then He clothed it with a garment of water; from this the moon became cooler than the Sun.'
ai.seo_question: Why is the Sun hotter than the moon according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) in *Al-Khisal* elucidates the physical composition of celestial bodies, attributing the Sun's intense heat to its seven layers being clothed in fire, while the Moon's coolness stems from being clothed in water. This cosmological model reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of integrating revealed knowledge with observable natural phenomena, offering a metaphysical explanation for thermal differences. It underscores the divine wisdom in creation, where material elements are layered to serve specific functional purposes within the universe.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-40 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Isa ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Ali ibn Mahzyar, on the authority of Ali ibn Hisan, on the authority of Abi Ayoob, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Muslim, “I asked Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB), ‘May I be your ransom! Why is the Sun hotter than the moon?’ Then he (MGB) replied, ‘Indeed the Blessed the Sublime God created the Sun from layers of the light of fire and pure gaseous water one layer of each upon the other until the seventh layer which can be seen and is made of fire. Thus, the heat of the Sun is more than that of the moon.’ I asked, ‘How about the moon?’ The Imam (MGB) replied, ‘The Sublime God has made the moon from layers of the light of fire and gaseous vapors one upon another for seven layers and has covered up the seventh layer with water. That is why the moon is cooler than the Sun.’
